findings.title: Sync session cannot see uncommitted user row — fix never creates budget allocations
findings.problem: _sync_budget_for_idp_projects opens a new sync session via get_session() while db_user was inserted into the still-uncommitted outer AsyncSession passed to create_user_from_idp. On PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED, the new sync session cannot see the uncommitted user row. ProjectMemberBudgetAssignment.user_id carries a FK constraint to the users table, so every INSERT attempt fails with an IntegrityError, which is caught by the per-project try/except and silently swallowed.
findings.impact: The fix is entirely ineffective: no budget allocations are created for any service account on first Keycloak login. The exception is hidden, login succeeds, and the original bug (no budget records) persists unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Call _sync_budget_for_idp_projects after the outer session has committed. One approach: have create_user_from_idp return the db_user and project_names, then let the caller (which owns the session lifecycle) invoke _sync_budget_for_idp_projects after commit. Another approach: use an SQLAlchemy after_commit event hook on the AsyncSession.

findings.title: Synchronous DB calls inside async def block the asyncio event loop
findings.problem: _sync_budget_for_idp_projects is declared async def and awaited by create_user_from_idp, but its body executes synchronous blocking DB operations (get_session() context manager, session.exec(), session.commit()) per project name with no thread-pool offload.
findings.impact: The FastAPI asyncio event loop thread is blocked for the duration of each per-project sync DB round-trip during every first-login. Degrades concurrent request handling proportionally to the number of IDP-provisioned projects.
findings.recommendation: Offload per-project sync work to a thread pool: wrap the per-project body in a sync helper and call await asyncio.to_thread(helper, project_name, user_id). Alternatively, refactor _sync_project_budget_member_added to accept an AsyncSession and use get_async_session() as the existing _ensure_projects_exist already does.

findings.title: Concurrent first-login race-loser recovery path never calls budget sync
findings.problem: The IntegrityError recovery path in authenticate_persistent_user reloads the already-committed user via _sync_existing_user but never calls _sync_budget_for_idp_projects. If the race winner's budget sync also fails (e.g., due to CR-001), neither code path creates budget allocations for the user.
findings.impact: Service accounts whose first-login request loses a concurrent race skip budget bootstrap entirely, requiring manual UI removal and re-addition to remediate.
findings.recommendation: Add a _sync_budget_for_idp_projects call in the race-loser recovery branch after the user is reloaded, using the same outer try/except non-fatal guard as the create path.

findings.title: Outer except block omits exc_info=True, silently dropping the traceback
findings.problem: The call-site except in create_user_from_idp logs logger.warning(f'budget_sync_failed_on_idp_bootstrap: ...') without exc_info=True. If the helper raises before its inner per-project loop (e.g., ImportError from deferred imports, coroutine scheduling failure), the full stack trace is discarded. The inner per-project loop correctly uses exc_info=True.
findings.impact: Production incidents on this code path are uninvestigable from logs alone: only the exception message string is preserved, never the file/line stack that identifies the root cause.
findings.recommendation: Add exc_info=True to the outer logger.warning call: logger.warning(f'budget_sync_failed_on_idp_bootstrap: user_id={db_user.id!r} error={e}', exc_info=True).

findings.title: No tests exercise _sync_budget_for_idp_projects internals; critical FK bug passes undetected
findings.problem: Both new tests mock _sync_budget_for_idp_projects entirely at the class level. The per-project session lifecycle, commit ordering, FK timing, and exception isolation are never executed, which is why CR-001 (FK violation on every first login) passes the test suite without detection.
findings.impact: The implementation is entirely ineffective (CR-001) yet all tests pass. Future regressions in the per-project session logic will also be invisible to the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a focused unit test for _sync_budget_for_idp_projects that mocks get_session() and ProjectAssignmentService._sync_project_budget_member_added at the call level (not the whole helper), asserting: (1) session.commit() is called once per project, (2) a per-project exception is swallowed and the loop continues to the next project, (3) the warning log is emitted with exc_info=True for a per-project failure.
